results.name: outlier_vs_majority_neighbour_contrast
results.description: In sets of >= 3 examples with exactly one minority-parity example, yes rate for non-example targets within 3 of the outlier minus yes rate for minority-parity (rule-violating) non-example targets within 3 of a majority example; observed > null means the outlier's neighbourhood is privileged over mere proximity to other examples more than modelled, observed < null means people treat proximity to any example alike (interval-like) more than modelled.
results.code:
# name: outlier_vs_majority_neighbour_contrast
# description: In sets of >= 3 examples with exactly one minority-parity example, yes rate for non-example targets within 3 of the outlier minus yes rate for minority-parity (rule-violating) non-example targets within 3 of a majority example; observed > null means the outlier's neighbourhood is privileged over mere proximity to other examples more than modelled, observed < null means people treat proximity to any example alike (interval-like) more than modelled.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    par = np.mod(ex, 2)
    odd = np.nansum(par == 1, axis=1)
    even = np.nansum(par == 0, axis=1)
    one_out = (n >= 3) & ((odd == 1) | (even == 1))
    minp = np.where(odd == 1, 1, 0)
    is_out = (par == minp[:, None])
    dist = np.abs(ex - t[:, None])
    d_out = np.nanmin(np.where(is_out, dist, np.inf), axis=1)
    d_maj = np.nanmin(np.where(~is_out & ~np.isnan(ex), dist, np.inf), axis=1)
    a = one_out & (d > 0) & (d_out <= 3)
    b = one_out & (d > 0) & (d_out > 3) & (d_maj <= 3) & (np.mod(t, 2) == minp)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: lag1_response_autocorr
results.description: Correlation between consecutive responses within a session (sessions split where trial_index resets, rows ordered by trial_index); observed > null means responses are serially perseverative beyond what the trial-independent model produces.
results.code:
# name: lag1_response_autocorr
# description: Correlation between consecutive responses within a session (sessions split where trial_index resets, rows ordered by trial_index); observed > null means responses are serially perseverative beyond what the trial-independent model produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[0, (np.diff(ti) < 0).astype(int)])
    order = np.lexsort((ti, pid))
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()[order]
    p = pid[order]
    same = p[1:] == p[:-1]
    a, b = y[:-1][same], y[1:][same]
    if a.std() == 0 or b.std() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1])

results.name: single_example_near_far_gradient
results.description: For one-example sets, yes rate for targets 1-5 from the example minus yes rate for targets more than 20 away; observed > null means people's similarity generalisation from a lone example is steeper than the model's, observed < null shallower.
results.code:
# name: single_example_near_far_gradient
# description: For one-example sets, yes rate for targets 1-5 from the example minus yes rate for targets more than 20 away; observed > null means people's similarity generalisation from a lone example is steeper than the model's, observed < null shallower.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    a = (n == 1) & (d >= 1) & (d <= 5)
    b = (n == 1) & (d > 20)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: example_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate when the target is itself one of the shown examples; observed > null means people endorse the given examples more reliably than the model (its exception/noise mass leaves too much doubt), observed < null less.

# name: example_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate when the target is itself one of the shown examples; observed > null means people endorse the given examples more reliably than the model (its exception/noise mass leaves too much doubt), observed < null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()

    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)

results.name: shared_last_digit_distant_extension
results.description: Among sets of >= 2 examples all ending in the same digit, yes rate for non-example targets ending in that digit and more than 5 from every example; observed > null means people extend "ends in d" rules to distant numbers more than the model, observed < null less.
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_distant_extension
# description: Among sets of >= 2 examples all ending in the same digit, yes rate for non-example targets ending in that digit and more than 5 from every example; observed > null means people extend "ends in d" rules to distant numbers more than the model, observed < null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    ld = np.where(np.isnan(ex), np.nan, np.mod(ex, 10))
    same = (np.nanmax(ld, axis=1) == np.nanmin(ld, axis=1)) & (n >= 2)
    m = same & (np.mod(t, 10) == np.nanmax(ld, axis=1)) & (d > 5)
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() else 0.0

results.name: mixed_set_inrange_yes
results.description: Among sets of >= 2 examples that share neither parity nor final digit, yes rate for non-example targets lying strictly between the smallest and largest example; observed > null means people fill in the examples' range (interval generalisation for rule-less sets) more than the model, observed < null less.
results.code:
# name: mixed_set_inrange_yes
# description: Among sets of >= 2 examples that share neither parity nor final digit, yes rate for non-example targets lying strictly between the smallest and largest example; observed > null means people fill in the examples' range (interval generalisation for rule-less sets) more than the model, observed < null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    par = np.mod(ex, 2)
    ld = np.mod(ex, 10)
    mixed = (n >= 2) & (np.nanmax(par, axis=1) != np.nanmin(par, axis=1)) & (np.nanmax(ld, axis=1) != np.nanmin(ld, axis=1))
    m = mixed & (d > 0) & (t > np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)) & (t < np.nanmax(ex, axis=1))
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() else 0.0

results.name: magnitude_scaled_neighbour_contrast
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets 2-6 from the nearest example when that example is >= 50, minus the same when it is <= 20; observed > null means generalisation widens with magnitude (log-like number line) more than the model's compression predicts, observed < null less.
results.code:
# name: magnitude_scaled_neighbour_contrast
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets 2-6 from the nearest example when that example is >= 50, minus the same when it is <= 20; observed > null means generalisation widens with magnitude (log-like number line) more than the model's compression predicts, observed < null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    idx = np.nanargmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    near = ex[np.arange(len(t)), idx]
    band = (d >= 2) & (d <= 6)
    a = band & (near >= 50)
    b = band & (near <= 20)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: parity_outlier_far_majority_yes
results.description: In sets of >= 3 examples with exactly one example of the minority parity, yes rate for non-example targets of the majority parity more than 10 from every example; observed > null means people extend the majority parity rule to distant numbers despite the exception more than the model, observed < null means the exception suppresses rule extension more than modelled.
results.code:
# name: parity_outlier_far_majority_yes
# description: In sets of >= 3 examples with exactly one example of the minority parity, yes rate for non-example targets of the majority parity more than 10 from every example; observed > null means people extend the majority parity rule to distant numbers despite the exception more than the model, observed < null means the exception suppresses rule extension more than modelled.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    par = np.mod(ex, 2)
    odd = np.nansum(par == 1, axis=1)
    even = np.nansum(par == 0, axis=1)
    one_out = (n >= 3) & ((odd == 1) | (even == 1))

    m = one_out & (np.mod(t, 2) == maj) & (d > 10)
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() else 0.0
